common.tagline: Your Guide to the Right Scheme

home.heroTitle: The right scheme for your dream — without the confusion.
home.heroBody: Direct loan applications are not accepted under the SC Channel Finance System. Funds reach you through Channel Partners. SchemeSathi matches you to the right scheme and the right partner, in minutes.
home.microCardBody: Small business projects up to ₹1.40 lakh. Quick, collateral-light support for self-employment.
home.termCardBody: Larger ventures up to ₹50 lakh. For manufacturing, services and agri-business projects.
home.educationCardBody: For students pursuing higher studies in India or abroad, based on course cost.
home.privacyNote: Your caste category and income details are used only to check eligibility. Nothing is shared with advertisers or analytics tools.
home.literacyTeaser: New to loans? Plain-language notes explain every term as you go.

whoCanApply.a: Any SC beneficiary looking for a loan under the SC Channel Finance System. You must have a project or course cost estimate and basic profile information.

directApplication.q: Can I apply directly to the government?
directApplication.a: No. Under the Channel Finance System, applications go only through registered Channel Partners — State Channelizing Agencies, banks, or NBFC-MFIs.

channelPartner.a: A Channel Partner is a registered institution (SCA, PSB, RRB, or NBFC-MFI) that verifies your documents, appraises your project, and forwards your application to the government.

documents.a: Typically you need Aadhaar, caste certificate, income certificate, project cost estimate, and education certificates. Specific requirements vary by scheme.

trackStatus.q: How do I track my application?
trackStatus.a: Log in to SchemeSathi and go to Track Application. You can see the current status, which partner it is routed to, and any actions needed.

schemeCost.q: Is there a cost for using SchemeSathi?
schemeCost.a: SchemeSathi is free to use. There are no fees for matching, calculating, or finding partners. You only pay the loan processing charges set by your Channel Partner.

how.title: How the money reaches you
how.intro: Under the Channel Finance System you cannot apply straight to a ministry. Your application travels a fixed route:

steps.s1: SchemeSathi checks your profile against scheme rules and tells you which scheme fits.
steps.s2: You pick a nearby Channel Partner that handles that scheme category.
steps.s3: The partner verifies documents, appraises the project and forwards the case.
steps.s4: Funds flow to you through that partner at concessional interest.

glossary.SCA_def: A state-level corporation (usually an SC/ST development corporation) that identifies beneficiaries and channels funds locally.
glossary.PSB_def: Government-majority banks like SBI or Bank of Baroda that sanction and disburse the loans.
glossary.RRB_def: Rural-focused banks sponsored by PSBs, covering villages and small towns.
glossary.NBFC_MFI_def: Non-bank finance companies specialising in small micro-loans, often with doorstep service.

literacy.concessional_body: Normal business loans charge 12–24% interest. Concessional scheme loans charge far less (about 6–10%) because the government supports part of the cost. Lower rate means lower monthly EMI.
literacy.moratorium_body: A waiting period after you receive the loan when you pay nothing back. It gives your project or studies time to start earning. Whether interest builds up during this pause depends on the scheme — the calculator shows both cases honestly.
literacy.channel_title: Channel finance vs. a direct bank loan
literacy.channel_body: In a direct bank loan, you negotiate alone at market rates. In channel finance, the government routes subsidised funds through partner institutions at fixed low rates — but only through them, never directly.
